findings.title: Empty updateMany will throw after writing calendar cache
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache finishes by calling SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}). Prisma rejects updateMany when data has no fields ("data argument must have at least one field"), and @updatedAt is not applied unless an update actually runs. Every successful Google cache fill (webhook refresh and fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache) will therefore throw after the cache write, failing the caller and never bumping SelectedCalendar.updatedAt.

findings.title: connectedCalendars query crashes when the user has no calendars
findings.body: The handler always calls getCacheStatusByCredentialIds with connectedCalendars.map(cal => cal.credentialId). For a user with zero connected calendars that array is empty, and Prisma rejects credentialId: { in: [] } (empty IN lists are invalid). The connectedCalendars query, which this settings page loads with suspense, then errors instead of returning an empty list.

findings.title: Deleting cache does not refresh cache status in the UI
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The parent passes onChanged through but does not refetch that query, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old "last updated" timestamp and "Delete cached data" until a full reload.

findings.title: Migration stamps every existing cache row as updated now
findings.body: updatedAt is added as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every pre-existing CalendarCache row is recorded as updated at migration time rather than when it was actually written. The new cache-status UI uses max(updatedAt), so all current Google calendar caches will appear freshly updated even if they are old or near expiry. The SQL comment also still claims the column has no default, which is the opposite of what the statement does.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on tsx, which is not installed
findings.body: The dev:cron script was changed from ts-node (a declared devDependency) to npx tsx, but tsx is not in package.json. yarn dev:cron will either fail or pull an unpinned tsx via npx, so the local cron tester no longer runs from the repo's locked dependencies.

findings.title: Webhook helper is macOS-only and writes the wrong env file
findings.body: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS syntax and fails on GNU sed, so the script cannot update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL on Linux. ENV_FILE is also ../.env relative to the current working directory, not apps/web/.env, so even a successful run does not update the env file Next.js actually loads and the tunnel URL is never used.
